text:
sanjay (ML Eval): nightly eval flagged a sharp increase in function-calling / JSON schema failures for rwd-7b-quant-v2 — failure rate up to 12% vs 0.9% baseline. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/evals/2026-03-17/func-calls
ci-bot: automated summary attached: 26 failing prompts, 3 clusters by error type (malformed JSON, wrong field types, missing required fields)
noah (Model Ops): confirmed on canary — I repro'd a few failures locally with docker image tag rwd-7b-quant-v2:2026-03-16-optim1
eva (Applied ML): can you paste a failing example? want to see if it's generation noise or systematic formatting issues
noah (Model Ops): here's one failing response (trimmed):
```
PROMPT: call function get_user({"user_id":"42"})
MODEL OUTPUT: {
  "status": "ok",
  "result": {
    "id": 42,
    "name": "Alex",
  },
}
```
noah (Model Ops): notice trailing commas + extra wrapper object — violates our schema (no trailing commas, result should be array for multi entries)
eva (Applied ML): that looks like tokenization/decoding truncation or repetition of punctuation. Did we change stop sequences or the tokenizer?
lee (Infra): quant build included a small tokenizer tweak to fix rare whitespace edge cases last week — pinged infra release notes: https://releases.redwood/quant/2026-03-15
ashley (QA): running a narrow eval: 1000 prompts through rwd-7b-quant-v1 vs v2, v2 fails 11.8% malformed vs v1 0.7% — reproduces on CPU decode too, so not only GPU kernel flakiness
sanjay (ML Eval): error clusters: 1) trailing commas / extra punctuation 2) missing required 'id' field (sometimes string instead of int) 3) function name mismatches (get_user vs getUser)
eva (Applied ML): suspect the quantization path changed logits distribution causing the model to emit extra punctuation tokens at structure boundaries. Can we confirm logits for comma/comma+bracket?
noah (Model Ops): I dumped token probs for a failing case — comma probability spikes weirdly at closing bracket. attaching small snippet: 
```
... 
token_probs: [0.02, 0.01, 0.65(, ), 0.21(\n), 0.11(})]
```
noah (Model Ops): also saw occasional nulled bytes in stream that look like bad decoding of 2-byte sequences on quant kernel
lee (Infra): the quant runtime change included a small memcpy optimization across KV cache pages. possible off-by-one when copying trailing separators. i'll revert that locally and run the batch tests
ci-bot: reproduced failing prompt set id=eval-func-schema-20260317 on rwd-7b-quant-v2, seed=42. Attached first 5 failures (ids: 183, 189, 207, 244, 301)
ashley (QA): quick triage: are failures concentrated on long responses (>300 tokens) or short ones?
sanjay (ML Eval): mostly short to medium (30-150 tokens). weirdly, structured responses that include arrays are hit more often
eva (Applied ML): plan: 1) block rwd-7b-quant-v2 from canary rollout 2) run targeted decode trace to capture logits + kv state for a few failing prompts 3) rollback canary to rwd-7b-quant-v1 4) open infra bug for memcpy/kv-copy optimization
noah (Model Ops): doing an immediate rollback on canary now, pausing deploys for that tag :hourglass_flowing_sand:
lee (Infra): started local bisect between commits around the tokenizer + kv memcpy patch. initial suspect commit 0f4a9d2
eva (Applied ML): I want to run a constrained decode where we force the model to output json using constrained generation (masking punctuation) to see if intrinsic model behavior or decode pipeline causing it
sanjay (ML Eval): I'll add failing prompts to an eval suite and run them against CPU FP16 baseline, quant-v1 and quant-v2. attaching nightly eval job id: nightly-20260317-789
ci-bot: created issue INFER-4123: "rwd-7b-quant-v2: JSON schema / function-call failures up from baseline" assigned to @lee, @noah, @eva
ashley (QA): test plan added to ticket: include end-to-end function-calling integration tests + run on different seeds + log JSON outputs to S3 for triage
eva (Applied ML): if root cause is memcpy bug revert and patch, we should still add a fallback in runtime to sanitize trailing commas before handing to caller — thin guard while we fix model/runtime
noah (Model Ops): agree. I'll add a quick sanitizer in the function-calling postprocess that attempts a tolerant JSON parse and emits telemetry when a sanitize occurred (we'll still fail on incompatible types)
lee (Infra): bisect shows behaviour changed after commit 0f4a9d2 -> 0f4a9d2^ patched memcpy optimization. pushing patch to revert and run full regression now
sanjay (ML Eval): great. once we have a fix candidate let's re-run the nightly eval subset (eval-func-schema-20260317) and confirm failure rate drops back to ~1%
ashley (QA): noted. will run regression once canary tag updated
eva (Applied ML): small note for product: this only affects quant-v2 variant. hosted API customers on non-quant models unaffected. will draft a short status message for #incidents if rollback doesn't clear it
noah (Model Ops): rolling back canary completed at 1763504920. monitoring logs and evals now
ci-bot: nightly eval rerun in progress (subset), job id nightly-rerun-1763504970
sanjay (ML Eval): last update: rerun results initial: v2 failure rate dropped to 1.1% after rollback candidate revert. keeping on watch. will update INFER-4123 with final numbers
ashley (QA): thanks team. tagging this thread in the ticket for audit. :white_check_mark:
